tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:

- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	# Plan: move Catalog Management from Redpanda to Apache Kafka
2	
3	AIP snapshot: `aip:snapshot:v1:4d8db6483e03a6564e593a3cbcf07bd1bcb7795c22bd975e95dd9e5ab11313a6`
4	(`get_binding_picture`, `catalog-management`, `local`, broker `kafka:sokol111-local` = the Redpanda
5	broker. Outcome **PARTIAL**, broker capture at 2026-10-28T11:55:58Z.)
6	
7	## What AIP shows and what the source confirms
8	
9	Event bindings that touch Catalog Management (rows of the binding picture):
10	
11	| Topic | Producer (declared) | Consumer | Crossing | Status |
12	|---|---|---|---|---|
13	| catalog.product.events | catalog, image | ecommerce-image-service | INSIDE | PROMISED_AND_OBSERVED |
14	| catalog.product.events | catalog, image | ecommerce-product-query-service | OUTBOUND | PROMISED_AND_OBSERVED |
15	| catalog.category.events | catalog | ecommerce-category-query-service | OUTBOUND | UNRESOLVED (PROMISE_COVERAGE_MISSING) |
16	| catalog.attribute.events | catalog | ecommerce-category-query-service | OUTBOUND | UNRESOLVED (PROMISE_COVERAGE_MISSING) |
17	| catalog.attribute.events | catalog | ecommerce-product-query-service | OUTBOUND | UNRESOLVED (PROMISE_COVERAGE_MISSING) |
18	| tenant.tenant.events | tenant | ecommerce-catalog-service | INBOUND | UNRESOLVED (PROMISE_COVERAGE_MISSING) |
19	| tenant.tenant.events | tenant | ecommerce-image-service | INBOUND | UNRESOLVED (PROMISE_COVERAGE_MISSING) |
20	| tenant.tenant.events | tenant | product-query, category-query | NONE | (not affected) |
21	
22	The three "UNRESOLVED / PROMISE_COVERAGE_MISSING" outbound rows are observed bindings that the
23	event catalog does not declare. They are real consumers and I treat them like the declared ones.
24	The local Helm values (`environments/local/values/*-query-service.yaml`) match them.
25	
26	AIP's limits that shape the plan:
27	- **CAPTURE_SCOPE_LIMITED**: the capture covers only configured groups. So PRE-01 lists *all*
28	  groups on Redpanda before the move. If an unknown group reads a topic that this plan doesn't
29	  cover, I stop.
30	- **PRODUCER_SIDE_DECLARED_ONLY**: AIP only declares producers and never observes them. The
31	  source code confirms them: `ecommerce-catalog-service-api/pkg/events/topics.go` lists the three
32	  catalog topics, and `ecommerce-image-service-api/pkg/events/topics.go` shows the image service
33	  writes to `catalog.product.events`.
34	- AIP never establishes delivery between brokers. I check the bridge only with broker tools.
35	
36	During planning I could not run `rpk`, `docker` or `kubectl` because those calls were denied. So
37	partition counts, the full group list, replica counts and the Kafka listener inside the container
38	are not known yet. PRE-01 reads them first.
39	
40	## Topology after the move
41	
42	- **Kafka** gets the producers of `catalog.product.events`, `catalog.category.events` and
43	  `catalog.attribute.events` (catalog, image) and the consumers of `tenant.tenant.events` (catalog,
44	  image) and `catalog.product.events` (image).
45	- **Redpanda** keeps `tenant.tenant.events` (producer: tenant service) and the consumers
46	  product-query and category-query.
47	
48	So there are two MM2 flows, and they share no topics:
49	
50	| Flow | Topics |
51	|---|---|
52	| redpanda -> kafka | `tenant.tenant.events` |
53	| kafka -> redpanda | `catalog.product.events`, `catalog.category.events`, `catalog.attribute.events` |
54	
55	No topic is mirrored both ways. `IdentityReplicationPolicy` keeps topic names, so the consumers
56	need no change. That policy cannot detect loops, which is why the disjoint allow-lists matter.
57	Heartbeats are also turned off, so MM2 creates no `heartbeats` topic for the two flows to copy back
58	and forth.
59	
60	**Not mirrored:** `tenant.tenant.events.dlq`. Catalog and image write their DLQ messages for
61	tenant events to `<topic>.dlq` (`commons/pkg/kafka/config/defaults.go:61`), so after the move
62	their DLQ messages land on Kafka. AIP shows no consumer of this DLQ. PRE-01 checks Redpanda for
63	one, and if one exists I stop rather than add a flow without an amendment.
64	
65	## Sequence and why
66	
67	1. **PRE-01 / PRE-02.** Read-only checks, then back up the two ConfigMaps and the replica counts.
68	   Tilt deployed with `helm template` + `k8s_yaml`, so there is no Helm release to upgrade. The
69	   live ConfigMap `<name>-config` is what the pods read.
70	2. **KAFKA-01.** Create the three catalog topics on Kafka with the same partition counts as on
71	   Redpanda. The producers allow auto-creation, which would use broker defaults and could change
72	   which partition a key goes to.
73	3. **MM2-01 / MM2-02.** Run one dedicated MM2 process (`catalog-move-mm2`, host image by digest,
74	   on `shared-network`) with both flows. The redpanda->kafka flow also emits checkpoints and syncs
75	   group offsets, only for `ecommerce-catalog-service` and `ecommerce-image-service`, and with
76	   `offset-syncs.topic.location=target` so MM2 writes nothing to Redpanda for that flow. Checkpoints
77	   follow the flow's topic list, so the image group's Redpanda offsets on `catalog.product.events`
78	   are not copied onto Kafka's new, separate topic.
79	4. **CHK-01.** `tenant.tenant.events` on Kafka has caught up with Redpanda, and MM2 has tasks for
80	   the catalog topics.
81	5. **CUT-01.** Stop catalog first. Its outbox keeps unsent events in MongoDB, and they publish to
82	   Kafka after restart. Then let the image service drain `catalog.product.events` on Redpanda to lag
83	   0 and stop it. This step matters because the Kafka copy of that topic starts empty. Seeding it
84	   from Redpanda would mean mirroring the topic in both directions.
85	6. **CHK-02.** Both groups have translated offsets on Kafka `tenant.tenant.events`, so they
86	   continue where they stopped instead of replaying from `earliest`. Translation is conservative: it
87	   may point earlier, which means some events get delivered again. It never points past unread
88	   events.
89	7. **CUT-02.** Set `kafka.brokers: "kafka:29092"` in both ConfigMaps and scale back up. One
90	   setting covers the producer, the consumers and the DLQ producer.
91	8. **CHK-03, TEST-01, REPORT-01.** Check the consumers on both brokers and ask the operator for
92	   the functional test. The MM2 bridge stays running; it is part of the target state.
93	
94	Any failed check stops the run and is reported.
95	
96	## What this plan creates (and so may later remove)
97	
98	- Kafka topics `catalog.product.events`, `catalog.category.events`, `catalog.attribute.events`.
99	  `tenant.tenant.events` and `tenant.tenant.events.dlq` appear on Kafka through MM2 and the
100	  services.
101	- Container `catalog-move-mm2`.
102	- MM2 internal topics. On Kafka: `mm2-configs/offsets/status.redpanda.internal`,
103	  `redpanda.checkpoints.internal`, `mm2-offset-syncs.kafka.internal`. On Redpanda:
104	  `mm2-configs/offsets/status.kafka.internal`. PRE-01 checks that none of these exist before the
105	  move.
106	- Kafka consumer-group offsets for the two moved groups.
107	- Workspace files `mm2/`, `backup/`, `patched/`.
108	- Changed: the ConfigMaps `ecommerce-catalog-service-config` and `ecommerce-image-service-config`.
109	  The repo values files are not edited.
110	
111	Nothing is deleted in this plan. Before anything created is removed later, I check it by name
112	against this list.
113	
114	## Rollback (only if the operator asks; recorded as an amendment)
115	
116	1. Scale both services to 0.
117	2. Apply the `backup/` ConfigMaps and scale back to the saved replica counts.
118	
119	Events produced on Kafka in the meantime have already been mirrored to Redpanda. The image group's
120	old Redpanda offset on `catalog.product.events` is then behind, so those events are delivered
121	again.
122	
123	## Delivery guarantees
124	
125	The move gives at-least-once delivery at best. Some events may be delivered again: offset
126	translation is conservative and MM2 can redeliver on restart. Ordering is kept per partition
127	within each topic. The two brokers also stay mixed for a while, because catalog topics on Redpanda
128	hold pre-move records written directly and post-move records mirrored from Kafka. I make no claim
129	that the move is lossless or exactly-once. The query services' versioned projections
130	(product-update-flow.md) tolerate duplicates and out-of-order messages, but that is their design,
131	not something the move guarantees.

content.text:
# Stopped at CHK-01: the kafka→redpanda flow isn't running

I stopped before the cutover. Both services are still on Redpanda with 1/1 pods ready, and all four Redpanda consumer groups are Stable with lag 0, so no consumer has lost events.

## What failed
In the MirrorMaker 2 log, both connectors of the **kafka→redpanda** flow were rejected at startup:
```
MirrorSourceConnector can't setup offset-syncs feature while emit.offset-syncs.enabled set to false
MirrorCheckpointConnector can't run without offset syncs
MirrorCheckpointConnector can't run with emit.checkpoints.enabled set to false
```
The planned setting `kafka->redpanda.emit.offset-syncs.enabled = false` isn't accepted. MM2 4.1.2 refuses to run the source connector that way, and that connector is the one that copies the three `catalog.*` topics back to Redpanda for the product-query and category-query services. If I had cut over, those services would have stopped getting catalog events.

CHK-01 also turned up things that don't match what the plan said MM2 would create:
- **Heartbeat topics:** `heartbeats` now exists on both brokers and `redpanda.heartbeats` on Kafka, even with `emit.heartbeats.enabled=false`. All of them are empty, and neither allow-list includes them, so nothing is mirrored in both directions.
- **Offset-syncs topic name:** it's `mm2-offset-syncs.redpanda.internal` on Kafka; the plan expected `mm2-offset-syncs.kafka.internal`.
- **Worker group:** MM2 also created a group `kafka-mm2` on Redpanda.

## What did work
- **PRE-01:** Redpanda's groups are exactly the four AIP lists. There's no `tenant.tenant.events.dlq` and no MM2 topics existed beforehand. All topics have 1 partition, Kafka was empty and the Kafka image digest is on the host.
- **PRE-02:** the two ConfigMaps and the replica counts (1 and 1) are saved in `backup/`.
- **KAFKA-01:** the three `catalog.*` topics are on Kafka with 1 partition each.
- **MM2-01 / MM2-02:** `mm2/mm2.properties` is written and the container `catalog-move-mm2` is running.
- **redpanda→kafka flow:** `tenant.tenant.events` on Kafka is at end offset 1, the same as Redpanda. Kafka also has offsets for the groups `ecommerce-catalog-service` and `ecommerce-image-service` (not yet checked; that's CHK-02).

## Amendments
`amendments.json` has one entry. The plan's `kafka-*.sh` commands pointed at `localhost:9092` inside the `kafka` container, but nothing listens there. The working address is `localhost:19092`, which is what the container's own config advertises.

## State left as it is
I deleted nothing. Still in place: the container `catalog-move-mm2` (redpanda→kafka is mirroring, kafka→redpanda is not), the Kafka topics and MM2 internal topics listed above, the Kafka group offsets, and the workspace folders `mm2/` and `backup/`. I didn't change either ConfigMap and didn't scale either Deployment.

## Possible fix (your call; it would be a new amendment)
1. Remove `kafka->redpanda.emit.offset-syncs.enabled`.
2. Set `kafka->redpanda.offset-syncs.topic.location = target`. Without this, that flow's offset-syncs topic would also be named `mm2-offset-syncs.redpanda.internal` on Kafka, the same topic the redpanda→kafka flow already uses.
3. Restart `catalog-move-mm2` and run CHK-01 again.

The flow's checkpoint connector might still log an error while checkpoints are off. That should be harmless, but I haven't tested it.

I make no claim that the move so far is lossless or exactly-once. Shall I go ahead with this fix?

content.text:
# Stopped again at CHK-01: `heartbeats` was mirrored in both directions

## What the fix did
I applied it and recorded it in `amendments.json` (13:25:03Z). In `mm2/mm2.properties` I removed `kafka->redpanda.emit.offset-syncs.enabled` and added `kafka->redpanda.offset-syncs.topic.location = target`. Then I restarted `catalog-move-mm2` and ran CHK-01 again.

- **Fixed:** the kafka→redpanda flow now runs and copies `catalog.product.events`, `catalog.category.events` and `catalog.attribute.events`.
- **Expected error:** the only error left in the log is the checkpoint connector rejection (`can't run with emit.checkpoints.enabled set to false`). That flow has checkpoints off on purpose.

## The new failure
Each flow was also copying `heartbeats`, which is on neither allow-list:
```
replicating ... redpanda->kafka: [tenant.tenant.events-0, heartbeats-0]
replicating ... kafka->redpanda: [catalog.attribute.events-0, catalog.product.events-0, catalog.category.events-0, heartbeats-0]
```
MM2 adds heartbeat topics to a flow whatever its allow-list says. With `IdentityReplicationPolicy` the topic has the same name on both brokers, so `heartbeats` was being mirrored both ways, which TASK.md forbids. The topic is empty on both brokers, so nothing looped. Before the fix this didn't happen, because the kafka→redpanda source connector never started.

## What I did about it
- I stopped `catalog-move-mm2` at 13:27:37Z to end the two-way mirroring. I didn't remove it, and I recorded the stop in `amendments.json`.
- I didn't reach CHK-02 or the cutover, and I didn't change any ConfigMap or Deployment.
- Both services and all four consumer groups are still on Redpanda and Stable. Since the bridge is stopped, nothing is being mirrored now.

## What's left in place
I deleted nothing. Still there:
- the stopped container `catalog-move-mm2`
- on Kafka: the three `catalog.*` topics and `tenant.tenant.events`, plus MM2's internal and heartbeat topics, and the offsets for the two moved groups
- on Redpanda: MM2's internal topics, `heartbeats` and the group `kafka-mm2`
- in the workspace: `mm2/` and `backup/`

`amendments.json` lists all of these.

## Decision needed
Every flow in this MM2 version mirrors `heartbeats`, so the plan's design can't meet the "no topic in both directions" rule. Options, none of them tested yet:
1. **Rename topics on one side:** use `DefaultReplicationPolicy`, where mirrored topics get a prefix (e.g. `kafka.catalog.product.events`). The Redpanda query services would then need their topic config changed.
2. **One-way bridge only:** run only the kafka→redpanda flow and move `tenant.tenant.events` some other way. That would change the plan a lot.
3. **Stop the heartbeat copy:** find a supported MM2 setting that stops heartbeat topics being added, or gives them different names. I haven't confirmed such a setting exists in 4.1.2.

I make no claim that anything so far is lossless or exactly-once. How do you want to proceed?

content.text:
The heartbeat problem is fixed and checked, and the cutover is done: both Catalog Management services now run on Kafka. One part of the final check is still open, and it needs the functional test.

**The fix:** I set `heartbeats.replication.enabled = false` in `mm2/mm2.properties`. MM2 4.1.2 has this setting; it appears in MM2's own config dump with the default `true`. After restarting MM2:
- redpanda→kafka copies only `tenant.tenant.events-0`.
- kafka→redpanda copies only the three `catalog.*` partitions.
- **The 1.5 s overlap:** right after the restart, the tasks ran for about 1.5 s with the old stored config, `heartbeats-0` included, until MM2 replaced it. All four heartbeat topics are empty (end offset 0), so no heartbeat record was copied.

**Correction to my last report:** MM2 had been writing the heartbeat copies under new names (`redpanda.heartbeats` on Kafka, `kafka.heartbeats` on Redpanda), so nothing went back to where it came from. `heartbeats` was still a source in both flows, which is why I removed it.

**Checks and steps since then:**
- **CHK-01 passed:** `tenant.tenant.events` is at end offset 1 on both brokers and the catalog flow has its tasks. The only error is the expected one from the checkpoint connector, which is off on purpose for kafka→redpanda.
- **CUT-01:** I stopped catalog, waited until image had read all 120 events on Redpanda's `catalog.product.events`, then stopped image.
- **CHK-02 passed:** on Kafka, both groups were at offset 1 on `tenant.tenant.events`, the same as on Redpanda, so they won't replay the tenant history. Image has no offset on Kafka's `catalog.product.events`.
- **CUT-02:** both ConfigMaps now point to `kafka:29092` (copies in `patched/`), and both Deployments are back at 1 replica.
- **CHK-03, the part that doesn't need traffic, passed:**
  - Both pods are Ready with no errors in their logs.
  - Both groups are active on Kafka.
  - product-query and category-query are Stable on Redpanda with lag 0.
  - MM2 has logged no errors since the setup finished.

**Still open:** no catalog event has been produced since the cutover, so I couldn't yet see one reach Redpanda through the bridge. I didn't inject test events, because the real consumers would process them. I'll check that with the functional test's traffic; this change of order is recorded in `amendments.json`, which now has 5 entries.

Delivery is at-least-once at best and some events may arrive twice. I make no claim that the move is lossless or exactly-once.

OPERATOR: please run the functional test

# Done: Catalog Management now runs on Apache Kafka

`ecommerce-catalog-service` and `ecommerce-image-service` produce and consume on Kafka (`kafka:29092`). Every other service stays on Redpanda, and MirrorMaker 2 (container `catalog-move-mm2`) connects the two brokers. The functional test passed, and the last open check (catalog events reaching Redpanda) passed with the test's traffic.

## Final check (CHK-03, with the test's traffic)
- **Kafka → Redpanda:** the catalog topics grew on Kafka from 0 to 122 / 6 / 22 records (product / category / attribute). On Redpanda they grew by the same counts, from 120 / 4 / 20 to 242 / 10 / 42. So every event the moved services wrote arrived on Redpanda.
- **Redpanda → Kafka:** `tenant.tenant.events` is at 2 on both brokers.
- **Consumers:**
  - On Redpanda, product-query and category-query are Stable with lag 0 on every topic.
  - On Kafka, catalog is at lag 0 on `tenant.tenant.events`, and image is at lag 0 on both of its topics.
- **MM2:** running, with no errors since the 13:34Z restart. Each flow copies only its allow-list:
  - redpanda→kafka: `tenant.tenant.events`
  - kafka→redpanda: the three `catalog.*` topics
- **Functional test:** passed (run `s3r1`). In step 1 the first `GetProductById` call failed and the retry passed. That's consistent with the product event needing a moment to cross the bridge to product-query.
- **Log errors in the moved services:**
  - The 84 `not_found` RPC errors come from the operator's seeder job checking whether entities exist before creating them.
  - The profile-upload errors are failed connections to the observability service (`alloy`), which has nothing to do with the brokers.
  - The image service skips event types it has no handler for and logs a warning each time.
  
  None of them is broker-related.

## Plan changes (`amendments.json`, 5 entries, valid against the TASK.md schema)
1. **PRE-01:** the Kafka admin address inside the `kafka` container is `localhost:19092`, not `localhost:9092`.
2. **MM2-01:** removed `emit.offset-syncs.enabled=false` for kafka→redpanda (MM2 rejected the flow with it) and set `offset-syncs.topic.location=target`, so the two flows' offset-syncs topics don't end up with the same name.
3. **CHK-01:** both flows were copying `heartbeats`, so I stopped MM2 and reported.
4. **MM2-01:** set `heartbeats.replication.enabled=false`. Checked afterwards: no heartbeat partition is assigned, and all heartbeat topics are empty. For about 1.5 s after the restart, MM2 ran from its old stored config with `heartbeats` assigned, but no record was copied.
5. **CHK-03:** I checked the bridge part after the functional test, using its traffic, instead of injecting test events.

## What the move created (nothing deleted)
- **Container:** `catalog-move-mm2`. Leave it running; the Redpanda consumers depend on it.
- **On Kafka:**
  - the topics `catalog.product.events`, `catalog.category.events`, `catalog.attribute.events`, `tenant.tenant.events`
  - MM2's own topics: `mm2-configs/offsets/status.redpanda.internal`, `mm2-offset-syncs.redpanda.internal`, `redpanda.checkpoints.internal`, `heartbeats`, `redpanda.heartbeats`
  - the groups `ecommerce-catalog-service`, `ecommerce-image-service`, `redpanda-mm2`
- **On Redpanda:**
  - MM2's own topics: `mm2-configs/offsets/status.kafka.internal`, `mm2-offset-syncs.kafka.internal`, `heartbeats`, `kafka.heartbeats`
  - the group `kafka-mm2`
- **Changed:** the ConfigMaps `ecommerce-catalog-service-config` and `ecommerce-image-service-config` (`kafka.brokers`). The repository values files are untouched.
- **Workspace:** `mm2/`, `backup/` (the original ConfigMaps and replica counts, for rollback) and `patched/`.

## Delivery guarantees
The move gives at-least-once delivery at best. Events can be delivered again: MM2 may redeliver after a restart, and offset translation is conservative. Order is kept per partition. Redpanda's `catalog.*` topics now hold the records written there directly before the move, followed by those mirrored from Kafka after it. I make no claim that the move was lossless or exactly-once.

The architecture claims I relied on come from AIP snapshot `aip:snapshot:v1:4d8db6483e03a6564e593a3cbcf07bd1bcb7795c22bd975e95dd9e5ab11313a6`. I checked delivery between the brokers only with broker tools.
